stumbles.quote: Jev had done well on routing questions, so I expected it to do well here.
stumbles.why: Refers to prior Jev work on routing questions that the text never describes.

stumbles.quote: With the tic's definition from register.md in its prompt
stumbles.why: 'The tic' and register.md are never explained; it is unclear what a tic is or what the definition says.
declaude_lint is never explained; the reader cannot tell what the lint does or what a 'hit' is.

stumbles.quote: at a 5% error budget it could settle only 24.5% of hits
stumbles.why: 'Settle' and 'error budget' are not defined; it is unclear what counts as settling a hit or what the 5% applies to.

stumbles.quote: The bar we set in advance was 50%.
stumbles.why: The text never says what the 50% measures. It is implied to be the share of hits settled, but that is not stated.
The text does not say whether the 261 agreed labels are the ground truth for scoring. It also does not say how the other 39 hits were handled.
The counts total 105 hits, not 261 or 300. The text does not say which subset these come from, and the rule names are not explained.

stumbles.quote: It ranks the hits better than chance, but it can confidently decide too few of them to save a human any work.
stumbles.why: This conflicts with the section's later 24.5% result, since settling 24.5% of hits would save some work. 'Any work' overstates it.

stumbles.quote: Jev is a small decision model.
stumbles.why: Jev's origin and what it is are never explained. 'Oskar' also appears with no introduction.

point: Jev ranks lint hits better than chance, but it is poorly calibrated and settles only 24.5% of hits against a 50% bar, so it is not being added to public post review.
